text: When a subclass has its own init, it often still needs the parent's setup — and super is how you call it.
Vehicle sets up the number of wheels in its constructor.
Car adds a brand, but it still wants Vehicle's wheels — so it calls super dot init with four.
[chuckle] That runs the parent's constructor first, setting wheels, before Car adds its own brand attribute.
Without super, you'd have to copy the parent's setup by hand and risk it drifting out of sync.
[sniff] super works for any method, not just init — here describe extends the parent instead of replacing it.
It grabs the parent's description, then wraps it with the brand, building on top rather than starting over.
So the car reports both its brand and its inherited wheel count in one line.
[groan] super keeps your subclasses cooperative — they enhance the parent's behavior instead of duplicating it.
